gaps.text: In-line measurement of Temperature with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Fusion level: start with one model per method, then join the spectra with block scaling so neither method dominates. Both probes must look at the same small area of the medium, and the data must be aligned to a common time step. Each block needs its own calibration and diagnostics, and the fused model must beat the best single method on independent runs before the extra instrument is kept.)
No source gives detection limits or accuracy for glucose or lactate in cell culture media.
No source covers sterilisation, CIP/SIP or single-use bioreactor interfaces for these probes.

items.finding: The source states that a continuous process with a fixed probe location is meant to run in a steady-state window, which simplifies model design, lets calibrations be narrower and centred on the operational envelope, and allows validation on independent steady-state runs.
items.how_it_applies: This supports the fusion plan's requirement that the fused model be validated on independent runs: define a steady-state operating window for the cell culture pilot and validate the fused model on separate runs rather than on the calibration data.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The work concerns FT-IR and Raman in reactive liquid-liquid extraction for lithium recycling, not an aqueous cell culture matrix, and the probe geometry and process dynamics differ, so the modelling and validation approach would need re-testing here.

citation.quote: In contrast, a continuous process at a fixed probe location is intended to operate in a steady-state window, which simplifies the model design: calibrations can be narrower and centered on the operational envelope, validation can rely on independent steady-state runs, and online monitoring focuses on drift and out-of-specification detection rather than resolving the rapidly changing composition.
citation.label: E02 ¶8

items.finding: The source notes that typical drawbacks of any in-line method are maintenance and calibration effort, and that drift and aging can be handled by checking the baseline in each cycle of pure component phases and monitoring drift so one can react.
items.how_it_applies: This supports giving each spectral block its own calibration and diagnostics: plan periodic baseline checks and drift monitoring for each method before and after fusion, so a drifting block does not silently bias the fused model.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The recommendation comes from a lithium-recycling extraction process with defined pure component phases; a cell culture medium may not offer such clean reference phases, and the drift behaviour of the probes here is untested.

citation.quote: Potential typical drawbacks of any in-line method are maintenance efforts like calibration, and actions to sensor drift and aging could be easily overcome by checking the baseline in each cycle of pure component phases of process operation and monitoring any drift in order to be able to react.
citation.label: E02 ¶72

items.finding: The source reports a miniaturized electrochemical device with linear detection ranges of 0.5-35 mM for glucose and 0.5-40 mM for lactate and limits of detection of 0.18 ± 0.01 mM and 0.19 ± 0.01 mM in human induced pluripotent stem cell culture media.
items.how_it_applies: These figures give a reference for the concentration span and detection levels reported for glucose and lactate in a cell culture medium, which can help frame what the spectroscopy pilot would need to cover; they are not spectroscopic values and would have to be established separately for the pilot.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The device is electrochemical and microfluidic, the source is an abstract only, the matrix is hiPSC culture media, and measurements were made on serially collected small-volume samples rather than in line, so the numbers do not transfer to an in situ spectroscopic probe.

citation.quote: The device exhibits linear detection ranges of 0.5-35 mM for Glu and 0.5-40 mM for LA, with limits of detection (LODs) of 0.18 ± 0.01 mM and 0.19 ± 0.01 mM, respectively.
citation.label: E04 ¶1

dropped.finding: The source reports an amperometric sensor tested in cell culture media that achieved a detection limit of 1.41 ± 0.90 mM for glucose and 0.28 ± 0.17 mM for lactate.
dropped.how_it_applies: This offers a second, differently obtained set of detection limits for glucose and lactate in cell culture media, useful as a comparison point when judging whether the spectroscopy pilot's own detection capability is adequate; the pilot's limits would still need to be measured.
dropped.limits_and_transfer_risks: The sensor is electrochemical with enzyme-functionalised carbon nanotubes on gold electrodes, the source is an abstract only, and the measurements were chronoamperometric in cell culture media rather than in-line optical spectroscopy.

citation.quote: The sensor achieves a sensitivity of (4.67 ± 1.26) nA=(mM·mm2) and a detection limit of (1.41 ± 0.90) mM for the glucose, while it results in a sensitivity of (12.16 ± 3.8) nA=(mM·mm2) and a detection limit of (0.28 ± 0.17) mM for the lactate.
